sections.html:
Culpeper County covers about 383 square miles of Piedmont country at the base of the Blue Ridge. The seat is the town of Culpeper, and the three smaller towns are Boston, Elkwood and Reva. Population was 52,552 in 2020 and is estimated at 57,666 for 2025. The Rappahannock River forms the northeast border and the Rapidan the south.

Most local workers commute out, chiefly to Fairfax and Fauquier counties, so buyers often shop with the drive in mind. About 72.8 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. Main routes are US 15, US 29, US 211 and US 522.

Outside the town, communities include Brandy Station, Stevensburg, Jeffersonton, Rixeyville, Lignum and Richardsville. Houses inside the Town of Culpeper carry a town rate on top of the county's.

The county lists a 2026 rate of $0.37 for real estate plus $0.08 for fire and rescue, a total of $0.45 per $100 of assessed value. The Town of Culpeper adds $0.061. Three town service districts add to the town rate: Southridge at $0.03, Lafayette Ridge at $0.035 and Willow Shade at $0.02, as listed under 2025.

sections.h2: Due date and where to pay
sections.html:
The county collects once a year, on December 5. Mail your payment to Culpeper County Treasurer, PO Box 1447, Culpeper, VA 22701.

Ask the Treasurer about the penalty and interest before a payment is late. Selling in the fall? Have the closing agent confirm what is paid and how the December bill gets split with the buyer.

Culpeper assesses every two years, on a biennial cycle set by the Board of Supervisors. The current assessment became effective January 1, 2025 and stays in effect until January 1, 2027, with general reassessments falling in odd years.

The Department of Real Estate Assessments uses one or more of three methods:

  • Sales comparison: recent sales of similar properties, adjusted for size, condition, age, location and amenities.
  • Cost: current materials, labor and depreciation, plus the value of comparable vacant land.
  • Income: industry figures on what a property could earn and what it costs to run.

The same office runs the land use program, which must be revalidated at each general reassessment, and tax relief for elderly and disabled owners and certain surviving spouses.

During a reassessment, the formal route is the Board of Equalization, an independent body appointed by the Circuit Court. It may raise, lower or keep your value.

For each general reassessment the Board of Supervisors fixes when hearings start and the last day to apply, and the Board of Equalization works only in that window. The assessor can give you the dates for the next one.

After that, owners can apply to circuit court. Virginia Code 58.1-3984 lets an aggrieved taxpayer apply within the later of three years from the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date. The assessor's value is presumed correct for real property.

sections.h2: Using the valuation methods in an appeal
sections.html:
How the county got its number tells you which evidence to bring. Where it leaned on sales comparison, show recent sales of similar houses and note the differences in size, condition, age, location or amenities. If the cost method applies, a repair estimate that shows depreciation or a defect can matter. For a rental, income figures and operating costs speak to the income method.

Photos help under any method, particularly of damage that does not show from the street. Keep a copy of every page you send, with the date.

Two programs at the assessments office can change what a buyer pays. Land use enrollment has to be revalidated at each general reassessment, so if your acreage is in it, learn what a sale does to that status before signing. The same office handles relief for elderly and disabled owners and certain surviving spouses, and it can tell you whether your house is covered.

sections.h2: Working around a single December bill
sections.html:
One bill a year changes how a closing plays out. If you close in spring or summer, the December 5 payment usually falls to the buyer, yet your share of the year is still prorated, so expect to hand the buyer a credit. If you close after December 5, the bill should show as paid, and the closing agent will want the receipt.

Whichever side of the date you are on, get the Treasurer's status in writing and give it to the title company. A missed bill is the one thing that can hold up a settlement over a figure nobody has checked.

First, find out which rate applies to you: the county total, plus the Town of Culpeper rate and a service district if the house is in one. Second, ask the Treasurer for the paid status of the December 5 bill and for the mailing address for payments. Third, check the assessment, which is in effect from January 1, 2025 until January 1, 2027, and decide whether to wait for the next reassessment before you list. Fourth, ask the assessor about land use enrollment and relief. Finally, choose how to sell: with an agent, or by taking a direct offer on the house as it stands, which skips showings and lender approvals.

sections.h2: Tax and recording costs at closing
sections.html:
Property tax comes first in line. Under Virginia Code 58.1-3340 the lien outranks other liens until the tax is actually paid, sale proceeds must go toward taxes and levies, and a lien reaches the current year's rents too.

On the deed, the state's grantor tax is 50 cents per $500 of consideration (Virginia Code 58.1-802). The seller pays unless the buyer agrees to take it, and the clerk who first records the deed certifies that it was paid.

With one bill a year, the timing of a sale matters. A house that closes before December 5 leaves the question of who pays that bill, and the contract should say. Ask the closing agent to confirm the proration before you sign, and ask the Treasurer whether any earlier year is open.

If the house needs repairs or the commute makes it slow to sell, a direct as-is cash offer skips showings and lender approvals. The tax is still paid from the proceeds at closing, so get a payoff figure first.

faqs.q: What is the Culpeper tax due date?
faqs.a: December 5, once a year. Mail to Culpeper County Treasurer, PO Box 1447, Culpeper, VA 22701.

faqs.q: What is the Culpeper County tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: $0.37 for real estate and $0.08 for fire and rescue, a total of $0.45 per $100 of assessed value. The Town of Culpeper adds $0.061.

faqs.q: How often does Culpeper County reassess?
faqs.a: Every two years. The current assessment took effect January 1, 2025 and remains until January 1, 2027.

faqs.q: When can I go to the Board of Equalization in Culpeper?
faqs.a: Only in a general reassessment window. The Board of Supervisors sets the dates each time, and the assessor can tell you the next ones.

faqs.q: Does the seller or buyer pay Virginia's grantor tax in Culpeper County?
faqs.a: Normally the seller, at 50 cents for each $500 of consideration, unless both sides agree to a different split.
